answers.question: What does my plan have me doing this week, and why?
answers.text:
This week, your plan covers Monday, August 31 through Sunday, September 6. Here is the day-by-day outline:

- Monday, August 31: Full Body Strength A (strength) (a training day)  
- Tuesday, September 1: 35 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)  
- Wednesday, September 2: Rest day (a rest day)  
- Thursday, September 3: Full Body Strength B (strength) (a training day)  
- Friday, September 4: 35 minutes of easy jogging (a training day)  
- Saturday, September 5: Full Body Strength C (strength) (a training day)  
- Sunday, September 6: Rest day (a rest day)  

Why this week looks like this: You are beginning the Base phase of your long-term plan, which runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13. This is week 1 of the plan.  
Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13 (2 weeks). Build your lifting base and keep comfortable runs in place as you start this strength block.  
Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Strength (strength). Build your lifting base and keep comfortable runs in place as you start this strength block.  
Your recent jogging average over the prior complete weeks was 95.5 minutes per week, and this week's planned jogging total is 70 minutes, so the easy runs are meant to stay comfortable while you establish your lifting base.

answers.question: Is this week's plan a step up from what I've actually been doing?
answers.text: This week’s plan is not a step up in running volume: it schedules 70 min total jogging minutes, while your recent weekly average was 95.5 minutes. On the first day, you logged 0 m jogging minutes. The strength side, however, is a step up: the plan calls for Full Body Strength A (strength) on Monday, August 31, Full Body Strength B (strength) on Thursday, September 3, and Full Body Strength C (strength) on Saturday, September 5, whereas you recorded one strength session on Mon Aug 31 lasting 50.3 minutes. So the plan is a step down for running and a step up for strength frequency.

answers.question: What does my plan look like over the next few months?
answers.text:
Your long-term plan runs from Monday, August 31 to Sunday, November 22, spanning 6 phases and 12 weeks. You're currently in the Base phase, which started Monday, August 31 and runs through Sunday, September 13. The next phase begins Monday, September 14. This plan is built around your recent jogging baseline of 95.5 min.

Here are the phases:

- Base: Monday, August 31 to Sunday, September 13 (2 weeks). Build your lifting base and keep comfortable runs in place as you start this strength block.
- Build: Monday, September 14 to Sunday, October 4 (3 weeks). Strengthen the main movement patterns that will carry heavier loads later in the block.
- Recovery: Monday, October 5 to Sunday, October 11 (1 week). Absorb the first hard stretch with lighter movement and easy pacing to protect your progress.
- Build: Monday, October 12 to Sunday, November 1 (3 weeks). Return to tougher lifting with fresh legs and a more resilient base.
- Recovery: Monday, November 2 to Sunday, November 8 (1 week). Pull back briefly to let your body consolidate the hard weeks and stay durable.
- Maintain: Monday, November 9 to Sunday, November 22 (2 weeks). Keep your muscle and strength settled with consistent, controlled training.

And week by week:

- Week 1, starting Monday, August 31 (Base): key session Strength (strength). Build your lifting base and keep comfortable runs in place as you start this strength block.
- Week 2, starting Monday, September 7 (Base): key session Easy (run). Add steady gym progress without letting your easy runs become rushed.
- Week 3, starting Monday, September 14 (Build): key session Strength (strength). Strengthen the main movement patterns that will carry heavier loads later in the block.
- Week 4, starting Monday, September 21 (Build): key session Easy (run). Increase gym effort gradually while your easy runs stay relaxed and sustainable.
- Week 5, starting Monday, September 28 (Build): key session Strength (strength). Turn the early foundation into harder strength work without rushing the weight on your lifts.
- Week 6, starting Monday, October 5 (Recovery): key session Easy (run). Absorb the first hard stretch with lighter movement and easy pacing to protect your progress.
- Week 7, starting Monday, October 12 (Build): key session Strength (strength). Return to tougher lifting with fresh legs and a more resilient base.
- Week 8, starting Monday, October 19 (Build): key session Easy (run). Expand your capacity with controlled, sustainable strength sessions.
- Week 9, starting Monday, October 26 (Build): key session Strength (strength). Push your main lifts forward while using easy running to stay fit between sessions.
- Week 10, starting Monday, November 2 (Recovery): key session Easy (run). Pull back briefly to let your body consolidate the hard weeks and stay durable.
- Week 11, starting Monday, November 9 (Maintain): key session Strength (strength). Keep your muscle and strength settled with consistent, controlled training.
- Week 12, starting Monday, November 16 (Maintain): key session Strength (strength). Lock in the block and leave yourself ready for whatever comes next.
